page.layout: Running head at top, centred: "PROMPTU. ICONUM". Page number top left: 194. Two round medallion portraits with legends, side by side, above the text. One column of text in the centre, two entries, one per paragraph. A decorative ornament below the text, with no printed words.

main_text.l: IMP. SIGIS MVNDVS. AVG.
IMP. ALB ERTVS. AVG.
SIGISMVNDVS, Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Rex, Ven-
ceslai frater, mortuo Alberto communi omnium assensu Im-
perator creatur anno mundi 5372. à Christo nato 1410. Hic
Imperatoriæ planè indolis, sapientia, eruditione, probitate ac
liberalitate clarus, doctos fouit, ac dignitatibus ornauit. Atta-
men ab Amurathe Turcarum principe graui prælio victus, ca-
stris etiam exuitur. Hic per triennium magnam Europæ partem
peragrauit, quò schisma Christiano nomini calamitosissimum
extirparet: quare effecit ut reiectis adulterinis tribus Pontifici-
bus qui Barionæ sedem inuaserat, Od[illegible, ~2 letters]olumnius omnium
consensu Pontifex declararetur. obiit Sigismundus nulla reli-
cta virili prole, cum annos 27. imperasset. Vide Egna.li.3.
ALBERTVS Dux Austriacus, post Sigismundi obitum
Imperator designatur anno mundi 5399. à Christo nato 1437.
Hic Sigismûdi gener cùm esset, post eius obitum hæres regno-
rum Bohemiæ & Hungariâ factus est. Morauos ac Sarmatas in-
tra suos fines quiescere compulit. Bohemiæ factiones compe-
scuit: Amurathe Turcam, qui Hungariâ inuaserat, fugauit: Syn-
derouiam in deditionem accepit: inde in Græciam contendes,
Thessalonicam expugnauit. Austriam repetens, moritur anno
imperij sui (proh dura fata) secundo. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The ink blot covers part of the word after "Od" in the first entry, so two letters are unreadable and the name is given as illegible. The legends on the two medallions are partly cut off at the edges of the coins. I have copied them as far as they can be read, and the split between the left and right legends is uncertain. The ornament below the text carries no printed words. The running head is printed as "PROMPTV. ICONVM" and has been normalised to u as a vowel.
